title: Hardware Support
subtitle: Jeopardy Review

gradeLabels.f: F-RANK -- Back to the Anti-Static Bag

jeopardyFormatExample.clueText: This 7-pin data interface tops out at 6 Gbps and connects 2.5-inch SSDs and hard drives to the motherboard.

categoryLegend: Six PC-hardware domains: cables and connectors, motherboards and CPUs, RAM and memory, storage and RAID, power and cooling, and printers and diagnostics.

clues.clue: This USB standard, identified by its black port color, transfers data at 480 Mbps.
clues.explain: USB 2.0 introduced Hi-Speed data transfer at 480 Mbps and is commonly identified by black-colored ports. It remains widely used for keyboards, mice, and other low-bandwidth peripherals.

clues.clue: A SATA power connector has this many pins, supplying 3.3V, 5V, and 12V to drives.
clues.explain: The 15-pin SATA power connector carries three voltage rails: 3.3V (logic), 5V (electronics), and 12V (motor), replacing the older 4-pin Molex connector for modern drives.

clues.clue: This video connector carries no audio signal and uses an analog DE-15 plug that was standard on CRT monitors.
clues.explain: VGA (Video Graphics Array) outputs an analog signal through a 15-pin DE-15 connector and transmits video only, with no audio channel. It has been largely replaced by HDMI and DisplayPort on modern hardware.

clues.clue: This display standard supports 4K at 60 Hz on version 2.0 and jumps to 8K at 60 Hz on version 2.1, and it carries both audio and video.
clues.explain: HDMI 2.0 supports 4K resolution at 60 Hz while HDMI 2.1 adds support for 8K at 60 Hz and 4K at 120 Hz. Unlike VGA and DVI, HDMI carries both video and multi-channel audio over a single cable.

clues.clue: Thunderbolt 3 and Thunderbolt 4 both use this reversible 24-pin connector type and deliver up to 40 Gbps of bandwidth.
clues.explain: Thunderbolt 3 and 4 use the USB-C physical connector, providing up to 40 Gbps throughput, video output, and up to 100W power delivery (newer USB PD 3.1 allows up to 240W). The reversible 24-pin design means the connector cannot be inserted upside-down.

clues.clue: This largest standard desktop motherboard form factor measures 12 inches by 9.6 inches and supports up to 7 expansion slots.
clues.explain: ATX (Advanced Technology eXtended) boards measure 12 by 9.6 inches and offer the most expansion slots, up to 7 PCIe/PCI slots, making them the preferred choice for full-tower desktop builds.

clues.clue: On an Intel LGA1700 socket, the contact pins are located here, on the motherboard rather than on the CPU itself.
clues.explain: Intel uses the Land Grid Array design where the delicate pins are in the motherboard socket and the CPU has flat contact pads. AMD's AM4 platform used the opposite PGA design with pins on the processor.

clues.clue: A PC that resets its clock to the wrong date and time every reboot, and displays a CMOS checksum error, most likely has a dead version of this component.
clues.explain: The CMOS battery, typically a CR2032 coin cell, maintains the real-time clock and BIOS/UEFI settings when the system is powered off. A dead battery causes the system clock to reset and can generate a CMOS checksum error at POST.

clues.clue: Unlike legacy BIOS, this firmware standard supports GPT partition tables, graphical mouse-driven interfaces, and the Secure Boot feature.
clues.explain: UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) replaced legacy BIOS and supports GPT disks (which break the 2 TB MBR limit), provides a graphical setup interface, and enables Secure Boot to prevent unauthorized bootloaders from running.

clues.clue: This smallest common desktop form factor, measuring roughly 6.7 inches square, supports only one PCIe expansion slot and two DIMM slots.
clues.explain: Mini-ITX boards are designed for compact builds and are constrained to a single PCIe x16 slot and two DIMM memory slots. MicroATX is the mid-range option, supporting up to 4 expansion slots.

clues.clue: This smaller form factor of RAM module, used in laptops and compact systems, is named with an 'SO-' prefix.
clues.explain: SO-DIMM (Small Outline Dual In-line Memory Module) is approximately half the length of a standard DIMM and is the standard memory form factor for laptops, mini-PCs, and many all-in-one systems.

clues.clue: DDR4 RAM operates at this voltage, lower than DDR3's 1.5V, reducing power consumption and heat.
clues.explain: DDR4 reduced the standard operating voltage from DDR3's 1.5V to 1.2V, improving power efficiency. DDR5 takes this further to 1.1V while adding on-die ECC. Both DDR4 and DDR5 share the same 288-pin count.

clues.clue: To enable dual-channel memory mode on most motherboards, a matched pair of DIMMs should be installed in slots labeled with this color pairing, typically A2 and B2.
clues.response: What are the matching-color slots (A2 and B2)?
clues.explain: Dual-channel mode doubles the effective memory bandwidth by using two RAM sticks simultaneously. Most motherboards require the sticks to be in matching slots, typically A2 and B2 (the second slot of each channel), leaving A1 and B1 open.

clues.clue: This type of server RAM uses a ninth chip per rank to detect and correct single-bit memory errors, providing greater reliability than standard unbuffered modules.
clues.explain: ECC (Error-Correcting Code) memory adds a ninth chip per rank that stores parity data, allowing the system to detect and correct single-bit errors automatically. It is standard in servers and workstations where memory reliability is critical.

clues.clue: DDR5 introduced this feature built directly onto each DIMM, offloading error checking from the CPU memory controller and improving reliability at higher speeds.
clues.explain: DDR5 includes on-die ECC within each DRAM chip itself, separate from system-level ECC. This internal error correction helps maintain data integrity at the higher speeds and tighter tolerances DDR5 operates under, even in consumer non-ECC systems.

clues.clue: This RAID level stripes data across two or more drives for performance but provides zero fault tolerance, meaning one drive failure loses all data.
clues.explain: RAID 0 writes data in alternating stripes across all member drives, multiplying sequential throughput, but there is no redundancy. A single drive failure destroys the entire array, making RAID 0 suitable only for scratch space or caches.

clues.clue: Unlike a hard disk drive, an SSD should NEVER have this Windows maintenance utility run on it because it causes unnecessary write cycles that reduce the drive's lifespan.
clues.explain: Defragmentation was designed for spinning hard drives to consolidate fragmented files and reduce seek time. SSDs have no moving parts and access any block equally fast, so defragmentation only wastes program/erase cycles, shortening the drive's life. The TRIM command handles SSD block reclamation instead.

clues.clue: An M.2 2280 drive using the Key M edge connector and the NVMe protocol can reach sequential read speeds of approximately this many MB/s on a PCIe Gen 4 interface.
clues.explain: PCIe Gen 4 NVMe M.2 drives, such as the Samsung 980 Pro and WD Black SN850, achieve sequential reads near 7,000 MB/s. PCIe Gen 3 tops out around 3,500 MB/s, and PCIe Gen 5 pushes toward 14,000 MB/s.

clues.clue: This RAID level uses distributed parity across all member drives and can survive exactly one drive failure, while providing N-minus-1 usable capacity.
clues.explain: RAID 5 distributes parity information across all drives in the array rather than dedicating a parity drive, so the failure of any single drive can be recovered. With N drives, the usable capacity is N-1 drives. A second drive failure before the array is rebuilt results in data loss.

clues.clue: This RAID level can survive the simultaneous failure of any TWO drives in the array by storing two independent sets of distributed parity data.
clues.explain: RAID 6 extends RAID 5 by writing two separate parity calculations (P and Q) across all member drives, allowing the array to survive two simultaneous drive failures. Usable capacity is N-2 drives, and it requires a minimum of 4 drives.

clues.clue: This PSU voltage rail, which carries the majority of the wattage in a modern system, powers both the CPU and the discrete GPU.
clues.explain: Modern CPUs and GPUs draw the bulk of their power from the +12V rail. The +5V and +3.3V rails primarily supply logic chips, USB ports, and storage devices. High-end PSUs often carry multiple +12V rails to handle the current safely.

clues.clue: This type of UPS, the most affordable, stays idle during normal operation and switches to battery only after detecting a power loss, resulting in a brief transfer time.
clues.explain: A standby UPS passes utility power directly to the load and only switches to its internal inverter when it detects a power failure. The short transfer time is acceptable for most desktop PCs, though sensitive equipment may require a line-interactive or online UPS.

clues.clue: This UPS topology continuously runs all power through its inverter and charger, resulting in zero transfer time and the cleanest power output, making it ideal for servers.
clues.response: What is an online double-conversion UPS?
clues.explain: An online double-conversion UPS constantly converts AC to DC to charge the battery, then converts DC back to AC for the load. Because the load never runs on raw utility power, there is zero switchover time and complete isolation from power quality issues.

clues.clue: When applying thermal paste between a CPU and its heatsink, technicians recommend using approximately this amount, roughly the size of a pea or a grain of rice, centered on the IHS.
clues.explain: Applying too little thermal paste leaves air gaps that increase thermal resistance, while too much can overflow onto the motherboard socket. The correct pea-size or rice-grain amount spread by the heatsink's mounting pressure creates an optimal thin, gap-filling layer.

clues.clue: A surge protector's ability to absorb energy from voltage spikes is rated in this unit, and higher values indicate greater protection capacity before the MOVs are consumed.
clues.explain: Metal Oxide Varistors (MOVs) inside surge protectors clamp voltage spikes by absorbing the excess energy and converting it to heat. The joule rating reflects the total energy capacity the MOVs can handle before they degrade and the surge protector no longer offers protection.

clues.clue: In the laser printing process, this component reaches approximately 200 degrees Celsius to permanently melt and bond toner powder onto the paper.
clues.explain: The fuser assembly applies heat and pressure to the paper after the toner has been electrostatically transferred from the drum. The high temperature melts the plastic particles in the toner, fusing them permanently into the paper fibers.

clues.clue: This bootable, OS-independent diagnostic tool is used to test RAM modules for errors by repeatedly writing and reading patterns across all installed memory.
clues.explain: MemTest86 runs outside of any operating system directly from a USB drive or CD, allowing it to test all physical RAM without OS overhead. It cycles through dozens of test patterns to identify faulty memory cells or timing issues.

clues.clue: Raw printing jobs are sent directly to a printer over TCP port 9100 using this protocol, also called JetDirect, which sends the print data with no conversion or spooling.
clues.explain: Port 9100 raw printing, originally popularized by HP JetDirect, sends print data directly to the printer with no translation layer. It is fast and simple but lacks job management. IPP (port 631) and LPD (port 515) are the two alternatives covered by CompTIA A+.

clues.clue: Before working inside a PC, a technician attaches this wrist-worn device to the chassis ground to prevent electrostatic discharge from damaging sensitive components.
clues.response: What is an ESD wrist strap (antistatic wrist strap)?
clues.explain: An ESD wrist strap connects the technician's skin to the chassis ground through a 1 megaohm resistor, equalizing the electrostatic potential between the technician and the components. This prevents the sudden discharge of static electricity, which can destroy CMOS chips, CPUs, and RAM without the technician feeling any shock.

clues.clue: This drive self-monitoring technology logs attributes like reallocated sector counts and spin-up time, giving early warning of impending mechanical or electronic drive failure.
clues.response: What is SMART (Self-Monitoring, Analysis, and Reporting Technology)?
clues.explain: SMART is built into virtually all modern HDDs and SSDs and continuously monitors internal health parameters such as reallocated sectors, uncorrectable errors, and temperature. Utilities like CrystalDiskInfo read SMART attributes and alert technicians before a catastrophic failure occurs.
